items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: the Whiteman at that time had two saxophones and a fellow by the name of Byers, Hale Byers, you know, the guy who played everything.

ctx.x: player and a trombone player came in with us and a saxophone player, so I had what, trumpet, trombone, first of all two saxophones and then there was a 4 and then piano, banjo and drums. That's seven instruments, and that was big, and this meant I had to pay another guy, another guy or two, so the prices go up and I used to get a few howls like that from the girls or from the other fraternities.

Well, you know, I was so interested and I wanted to develop this. I wanted to develop an orchestra because well, the bigger orchestras that I listened to, the Whiteman orchestra, the Ray Miller orchestra, they all had two saxophones. the Whiteman at that time had two saxophones and a fellow by the name of Byers, Hale Byers, you know, the guy who played everything.
